headline: Passengers waited two hours at baggage claim, then watched their suitcases come out covered in a brown sludge the airline later insisted was peanut butter.
reveal: Real. American Airlines flight 2609, Miami to Atlanta, November 16. Passengers on TikTok assumed the worst. The airline said a jar in someone's checked bag had liquefied and leaked, and apologized.

sources.title: Airline: Brown substance covering bags was peanut butter, not poop
What was that mysterious brown substance covering dozens of bags at Atlanta airport?

author: claude

headline: A wildlife camera set up to watch for mink on a Baltic island filmed a deer with a single antler-like horn growing from the middle of its forehead.
reveal: Real. Saaremaa, Estonia. The Lutreola Foundation posted the clip: "Unicorn found in Saaremaa! Little girls' dreams have finally come true!" Experts still can't say what the growth is.

sources.title: 'Unicorn' deer caught on trail camera in Estonia

author: claude

headline: Two friends climbed to 20,593 feet on a South American volcano and played a full game of chess at the summit, wearing gloves, for a world record.
reveal: Real. Chimborazo, Ecuador. Guinness confirmed it this week as the highest-altitude board game, 200 feet above the old record from Nepal. Their plan if anyone beats it: go 200 feet higher.

sources.title: Highest altitude playing a board/party game
Two men scale Ecuador mountain for record-breaking chess game

author: claude

headline: After a 24-hour hunt with drones, commandos and baited traps for a lioness loose in a big city's suburbs, officials announced there had never been a lioness.
reveal: Real. Istanbul, this week. Thermal footage seemed to show a big cat in Sarıyer. Then the governor's office said new images showed it was not a lion or any large cat. They didn't say what it was. People posted their house cats.

sources.title: Officials: Animal spotted in Istanbul was not a lion
After Huge Hunt, Istanbul Says Nope, That Wasn't a Lioness

author: claude

headline: Worried pupils would skip class for a huge video game launch, a school entered every student who showed up both days into a draw for console gift cards.
reveal: Real. Belfast Boys' Model School, for the GTA VI launch on November 19, which landed on GCSE maths exam day. Two £70 PlayStation or Xbox cards. The letter home: Grand Theft Auto can wait until the weekend.

sources.title: School offers prizes to pupils for turning up to class on day GTA 6 comes out
School Offers Students $92 Reward to Keep Them From Skipping for GTA 6

author: claude

headline: Two lanes of a Florida highway were shut for hours after a truck lost 19 pallets of green peppers, scattering 11,400 pounds of them across the road.
reveal: Real. Palm Beach Boulevard, Fort Myers, November 17. Nobody was hurt. The sheriff's office called it a "pepper pileup" and couldn't resist a Peter Piper joke.

sources.title: Pepper pileup shuts 2 Palm Beach Blvd lanes in Fort Myers
'Pepper pileup': 11,400 pounds of peppers fall off semi

author: claude

headline: A zoo in Poland asked the public to stop mailing Christmas cards to its penguin colony after the birds received more than 3,000 letters in two weeks.
reveal: Made up. Zoos do get fan mail for famous animals, but these penguins are fictional.
author: claude

headline: An Italian hill village made its oldest donkey honorary deputy mayor after noticing it had attended more council meetings than two of the elected councillors.
reveal: Made up. Small towns really have elected dogs, cats and a goat as mayor. The donkey is still waiting for his turn.
author: claude

headline: A German supermarket chain apologized after a software update made its self-checkout machines wish every customer a happy birthday for an entire Monday morning.
reveal: Made up. Though anyone who has fought a self-checkout knows it is capable of far worse.
author: claude

headline: Police in New Zealand say a man reported his car stolen at 2 a.m., then officers found him asleep in its back seat three streets from his house.
reveal: Made up. A real Canadian did drive himself to a police station to report a lost phone this month and failed a breathalyzer in the car park, so the bar is high.
author: claude
